units.title: [AS] 1 Basic economic ideas and resource allocation

outcomes.text: Understand the different factors of production and their roles in producing goods and services.
Define land, labour, capital and enterprise as factors of production.
Distinguish human capital from physical capital.
Identify the rewards received by each factor of production.
Explain division of labour and specialisation.
Explain the entrepreneur’s roles in bearing risk and organising other production factors.

topics.title: 1.4 Resource allocation in different economic systems

outcomes.text: Understand how different economic systems allocate scarce resources.
Describe decision-making in market, planned and mixed economies.
Explain how market, planned and mixed systems allocate resources.
Use production possibility curves to analyse resource allocation, opportunity cost and productive efficiency.
Explain the meaning and purpose of a production possibility curve.
Explain PPC shapes representing constant and increasing opportunity costs.
Explain causes and effects of shifts in a production possibility curve.
Interpret the significance of a position inside, on or beyond a PPC.
Classify goods according to their economic characteristics.
Define free goods and private economic goods.
Define public goods.
Define merit goods and explain their under-consumption from imperfect information.
Define demerit goods and explain their over-consumption from imperfect information.
Explain scarcity as the fundamental economic problem.
Explain why individuals, firms and governments must make choices.
Define opportunity cost and explain how it results from choices.
Identify the basic resource-allocation questions: what, how and for whom to produce.
Understand scarcity, choice, opportunity cost, and the basic decisions about what, how and for whom to produce.
Explain why economics is classified as a social science.
Distinguish positive statements based on facts from normative value judgements.
Explain that ceteris paribus means holding other relevant factors constant.
Recognise the importance of distinguishing short-, long- and very-long-run periods.
Understand economics as a social science, distinguish positive from normative statements, and apply ceteris paribus across different time periods.

units.title: [AS] 2 The price system and the microeconomy

outcomes.text: Understand and calculate how strongly quantity supplied responds to price changes.
Define price elasticity of supply.
Use the PES formula to calculate price elasticity of supply.
Interpret percentage changes and the size and sign of the PES coefficient.
Identify factors affecting price elasticity of supply.
Explain how PES affects firms’ speed and ease of response to market changes.

topics.title: 2.4 The interaction of demand and supply

outcomes.text: Analyse how demand and supply interact to determine market prices and quantities.
Define market equilibrium and disequilibrium.
Analyse how demand and supply shifts change equilibrium price and quantity.
Explain joint, alternative and derived demand, and joint supply, across markets.
Explain price functions in allocation: rationing, signalling and incentivising.
Understand and calculate consumer surplus and producer surplus.
Explain the meaning and significance of consumer surplus.
Explain the meaning and significance of producer surplus.
Explain causes of changes in consumer and producer surplus.
Explain how PED and PES determine the extent of surplus changes.
Define effective demand.
Distinguish individual from market demand and supply.
Identify determinants of demand.
Identify determinants of supply.
Explain causes of demand-curve shifts.
Explain causes of supply-curve shifts.
Distinguish curve shifts from movements along demand or supply curves.
Understand effective, individual and market demand and supply; identify their determinants and distinguish curve shifts from movements along curves.

topics.title: 2.2 Price elasticity, income elasticity and cross elasticity of demand

outcomes.text: Define PED, YED and XED.
Use formulae to calculate PED, YED and XED.
Interpret percentage changes and the size and sign of PED, YED and XED coefficients.
Describe perfectly elastic, elastic, unitary, inelastic and perfectly inelastic demand.
Explain how PED varies along a straight-line demand curve.
Identify factors affecting PED, YED and XED.
Explain the relationship between PED and total expenditure.
Apply elasticity concepts to business and economic decision-making.
Define, calculate and interpret PED, YED and XED, including elasticity values, influencing factors, total expenditure and business decision-making.
Understand measures used to reduce inequalities in income and wealth.
Distinguish income as a flow from wealth as a stock.
Explain measurement of inequality using the Gini coefficient; calculation is not required.
Explain economic reasons for income and wealth inequality.
Evaluate redistribution through minimum wages, transfers, progressive taxes and state provision.

topics.title: 3.1 Reasons for government intervention in markets

outcomes.text: Explain government action to address non-provision of public goods.
Explain intervention addressing demerit-good over-consumption and merit-good under-consumption.
Explain reasons for controlling market prices.

topics.title: 3.2 Methods and effects of government intervention in markets

outcomes.text: Analyse the impact and incidence of specific indirect taxes.
Analyse the impact and incidence of subsidies.
Explain direct government provision of goods and services.
Explain maximum and minimum prices.
Explain buffer stock schemes.
Explain government provision of information.
Study government intervention methods and their effects on market outcomes.

topics.title: 4.2 Introduction to the circular flow of income

outcomes.text: Understand the basic circular flow of income between households, firms, government and overseas sectors.
Describe income flows among households, firms, government and the international sector in closed and open economies.
Explain injections and leakages in the circular flow.
Explain equilibrium and disequilibrium in the circular flow.

topics.title: 4.3 Aggregate Demand and Aggregate Supply analysis

outcomes.text: Use aggregate demand and aggregate supply analysis to examine national output and the price level.
Define Aggregate Demand.
Identify and explain consumption, investment, government spending, exports and imports in AD.
Identify determinants of Aggregate Demand.
Explain why the AD curve slopes downward.
Explain causes of shifts in the AD curve.
Define Aggregate Supply.
Identify determinants of Aggregate Supply.
Describe short-run and long-run AS curve shapes.
Explain causes of short-run and long-run AS shifts.
Distinguish movements along from shifts in AD and AS.
Explain equilibrium in the AD/AS model and its determination of output, prices and employment.
Analyse how AD and AS shifts affect real output, prices and employment.
Understand economic growth and how it is measured.
Define economic growth.
Explain how economic growth is measured.
Distinguish nominal GDP growth from real GDP growth.
Explain causes of economic growth.
Explain consequences of economic growth.
Understand unemployment, its measurement, types and consequences.
Define unemployment.
Explain unemployment measures and possible measurement difficulties.
Explain frictional, structural, cyclical, seasonal and technological unemployment.
Explain consequences of unemployment.
Understand price stability, inflation and deflation.
Define inflation, deflation and disinflation.
Explain CPI measurement and possible difficulties measuring price-level changes.
Distinguish nominal money values from real data.
Explain demand-pull and cost-push inflation.
Explain consequences of inflation.
Explain the meaning of national income.
Explain national-income measurement using GDP, GNI and NNI.
Adjust national-income measures from market prices to basic prices.
Adjust national-income measures from gross to net values.
Study the meaning, measurement and adjustment of national income statistics.
Understand how monetary policy influences economic activity and macroeconomic objectives.
Define monetary policy.
Identify interest rates, money supply and credit controls as monetary policy tools.
Distinguish between expansionary and contractionary monetary policy.
Use AD/AS analysis to assess how monetary policy affects income, output, prices and employment.
Understand how supply-side policies increase productive capacity and improve economic performance.
Explain supply-side policy through its effect on long-run aggregate supply.
Explain how supply-side policy aims to raise productivity and productive capacity.
Identify supply-side tools such as training, infrastructure and technological support.
Use AD/AS analysis to assess how supply-side policy affects income, output, prices and employment.
Explain how policy can pursue price stability, low unemployment and economic growth.
Use government policies to pursue price stability, low unemployment and economic growth.
Explain the meaning of a government budget.
Distinguish a government budget deficit from a budget surplus.
Explain the meaning and significance of national debt.
Classify taxes, distinguish marginal and average rates, and explain reasons for taxation.
Distinguish capital and current spending and explain reasons for government spending.
Distinguish expansionary from contractionary fiscal policy.
Use AD/AS analysis to assess fiscal-policy effects on income, output, prices and employment.
Understand budgets, debt, taxation and government spending, and assess expansionary and contractionary fiscal policy using AD/AS analysis.

topics.title: 6.3 Current account of the balance of payments

outcomes.text: Understand the components and significance of the balance of payments current account.
Identify current-account components and distinguish balance, deficit and surplus.
Calculate balances for goods, services, goods and services, and the current account.
Explain causes of current-account imbalances.
Assess domestic and external consequences of current-account imbalances.
Understand exchange rates and factors affecting their movements.
Define an exchange rate.
Explain how a floating exchange rate is determined.
Distinguish between depreciation and appreciation of a floating exchange rate.
Explain exchange-rate changes through currency demand and supply.
Use AD/AS analysis to assess how exchange-rate changes affect income, output, prices and employment.

topics.title: 6.5 Policies to correct imbalances in the current account of the balance of payments

outcomes.text: Understand policies used to correct current account imbalances.
Explain the government objective of current-account stability.
Assess how fiscal, monetary, supply-side and protectionist policies affect the current account.
Distinguish between absolute advantage and comparative advantage.
Explain the benefits of specialisation and free trade, including the trading possibility curve.
Measure the terms of trade and explain its causes and effects, alongside exports and imports.
Assess limitations of absolute and comparative advantage theories.
Understand why countries trade internationally, including the roles of comparative advantage, specialisation and free trade.
Explain protectionism in international trade.
Explain how tariffs, quotas, export subsidies, embargoes and administrative barriers affect trade.
Evaluate arguments supporting and opposing protectionism.
Understand protectionism, its main instruments, and arguments supporting or opposing restrictions on international trade.
Understand globalisation and its effects on economies, firms and individuals.
Explain globalisation, including its causes and consequences.
Distinguish free-trade areas, customs unions, monetary unions and full economic unions.
Explain trade creation and trade diversion.

topics.title: 11.1 Policies to correct disequilibrium in the balance of payments

outcomes.text: Describe the current, financial and capital accounts of the balance of payments.

subtopics.title: Policies Affecting the Balance of Payments

outcomes.text: Assess how fiscal, monetary, supply-side, protectionist and exchange-rate policies affect the balance of payments.
Distinguish expenditure-switching policies from expenditure-reducing policies.
Analyse balance of payments accounts and assess fiscal, monetary, supply-side, protectionist, exchange-rate and expenditure policies for correcting disequilibrium.
Distinguish nominal from real exchange rates and explain trade-weighted exchange rates.
Explain exchange-rate determination under fixed and managed exchange-rate systems.
Distinguish revaluation from devaluation of a fixed exchange rate.
Explain exchange-rate changes under different exchange-rate systems.
Analyse exchange-rate effects on the external economy using Marshall–Lerner and J-curve analysis.
Analyse exchange-rate measurement, determination and changes under different systems, including revaluation, devaluation, Marshall–Lerner and J-curve effects.
Classify economies according to their development level.
Classify economies according to national-income level.
Evaluate monetary, non-monetary and composite development indicators, including HDI, MEW, MPI and the Kuznets curve.
Compare economic growth rates and living standards across time and between countries.
Understand how economies are classified, measure living standards and development, and compare growth and living standards across countries and over time.

topics.title: 11.4 Characteristics of countries at different levels of development

outcomes.text: Analyse population growth and structure, including demographic rates, migration, optimum population and urbanisation.
Calculate Gini coefficients and interpret Lorenz curves to analyse income distribution.
Explain employment structures and trade patterns in economies at different development levels.
Understand population trends, income distribution, employment structures and trade patterns in economies at different development levels.

topics.title: 11.5 Relationship between countries at different levels of development

outcomes.text: Explain aid forms, motivations, effects and importance.
Explain the significance of trade and investment between countries at different development levels.
Define multinational companies and assess their activities and consequences.
Define foreign direct investment and assess its consequences.
Explain causes of external debt and assess its consequences.
Explain the role of the International Monetary Fund.
Explain the role of the World Bank.
Understand how aid, trade, investment, multinational companies, foreign debt and international organisations affect developing economies.
Define and calculate total utility and marginal utility.
Explain diminishing marginal utility.
Explain the equi-marginal principle.
Derive an individual demand curve using utility theory.
Assess limitations of marginal utility theory and its rational-behaviour assumptions.
Understand and calculate utility, diminishing marginal utility, consumer equilibrium, individual demand, and limitations of rational marginal utility theory.
Explain indifference curves and budget lines.
Explain causes of budget-line shifts.
Explain income, substitution and price effects for normal, inferior and Giffen goods.
Assess limitations of the indifference-curve model.
Understand indifference curves and budget lines, their shifts, income, substitution and price effects, and limitations of the model.
Define productive and allocative efficiency.
State conditions for productive and allocative efficiency.
Explain Pareto optimality.
Define dynamic efficiency.
Define market failure.
Explain reasons for market failure.
Understand productive, allocative and dynamic efficiency, Pareto optimality, market failure, and the reasons markets may fail.

topics.title: 7.4 Private costs and benefits, externalities and asymmetric information

outcomes.text: Define and calculate social, private and external costs, including their marginal measures.
Define and calculate social, private and external benefits, including their marginal measures.
Define positive and negative externalities.
Explain positive and negative consumption and production externalities.
Explain deadweight welfare losses from positive and negative externalities.
Explain asymmetric information and moral hazard.
Use costs and benefits to analyse decisions.
Calculate and apply private, external and social costs and benefits; analyse externalities, welfare losses, asymmetric information, moral hazard and decision-making.

topics.title: 7.5 Types of cost, revenue and profit

outcomes.text: Explain short-run production, product measures, fixed and variable factors, and diminishing returns.
Define and calculate short-run cost measures and explain average- and marginal-cost curve shapes.
Explain long-run production, including the absence of fixed factors and returns to scale.
Explain the long-run average-cost curve and minimum efficient scale.
Relate economies of scale to falling average costs.
Distinguish internal and external economies of scale.
Distinguish internal and external diseconomies of scale.
Define and calculate total, average and marginal revenue.
Define normal, subnormal and supernormal profit.
Calculate supernormal and subnormal profit.
Understand short- and long-run production, costs, economies and diseconomies of scale, revenue measures, and different types of profit.
Identify perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition, oligopoly and natural monopoly.
Compare market structures by sellers, products, entry freedom and information availability.
Explain legal, market, cost and physical barriers to entry and exit.
Analyse firm performance, competition, collusion and contestability across market structures.
Define and calculate a concentration ratio.
Compare market structures, their barriers, firm performance, efficiency, competition, collusion, contestability, and concentration.
Explain why firms differ in size.
Explain organic growth and diversification as internal growth.
Explain integration methods, their reasons and consequences.
Explain conditions for effective cartels and their consequences.
Explain the principal–agent problem between owners and managers.
Understand why firms vary in size, how they grow internally or through integration, how cartels operate, and how differing owner-manager objectives create principal–agent problems.

topics.title: 7.8 Differing objectives and policies of firms

outcomes.text: Explain the traditional profit-maximising objective.
Explain survival, profit satisficing, sales maximisation and revenue maximisation objectives.
Explain degrees, conditions and consequences of price discrimination.
Explain limit pricing, predatory pricing and price leadership.
Relate price elasticity of demand to revenue on normal and kinked demand curves.
Analyse firms’ differing objectives and pricing policies, including profit, sales, revenue, survival, price discrimination and strategic pricing.
Assess measures for correcting market failure, including taxes, subsidies, controls, regulation and information.
Explain government failure, its causes and its consequences.
Evaluate government measures for correcting market failure, improving resource allocation and addressing government failure.
Distinguish between equity and equality.
Distinguish between equity and efficiency.
Distinguish absolute poverty from relative poverty.
Explain the poverty trap.
Explain policies promoting equity and equality, including benefits and universal basic income.
Understand equity, equality, efficiency, poverty, poverty traps, and policies that redistribute income and wealth.

topics.title: 8.3 Labour market forces and government intervention

outcomes.text: Explain labour demand as derived demand.
Identify factors affecting labour demand in a firm or occupation.
Explain shifts and movements along a labour-demand curve.
Define and calculate marginal revenue product and derive a firm's labour demand.
Explain wage and non-wage factors affecting labour supply.
Explain shifts and movements along a labour-supply curve.
Explain equilibrium wages and employment in a perfectly competitive labour market.
Assess how unions, minimum wages and monopsony affect wages and employment.
Explain wage differentials through labour-market forces.
Define transfer earnings and economic rent, and explain factors affecting them.
Analyse labour demand and supply, wage determination, labour-market intervention, wage differentials, transfer earnings, and economic rent.
Explain and calculate the multiplier, propensities, tax rates, national income and AD changes.
Explain AD components and their determinants, including consumption, saving, investment, government spending and net exports.
Explain full-employment and equilibrium national income, including inflationary and deflationary gaps.
Understand the multiplier process, Aggregate Demand components and determinants, and equilibrium national income including inflationary and deflationary gaps.
Distinguish between actual growth and potential growth in national output.
Explain positive and negative output gaps.
Explain business-cycle phases, causes and the function of automatic stabilisers.
Assess policies designed to stimulate economic growth and their effectiveness.
Define inclusive growth, assess its distributional effects and explain policies promoting it.
Define sustainable growth and assess resource use, environmental effects and mitigation policies.
Distinguish actual, potential and gap output; analyse business cycles, growth policies, inclusive growth, sustainability and environmental effects.
Define full employment.
Explain equilibrium and disequilibrium unemployment, including hysteresis.
Distinguish between voluntary and involuntary unemployment.
Define the natural unemployment rate, identify its determinants and discuss policy implications.
Analyse patterns and trends in employment and unemployment.
Explain geographical and occupational labour mobility and factors affecting it.
Assess policies intended to reduce unemployment and their effectiveness.
Understand full employment, unemployment types, hysteresis, natural unemployment, labour mobility, employment trends and policies to reduce unemployment.
Define money and explain its functions and characteristics.
Define the money supply.
Explain and apply the quantity theory of money, MV = PT.
Explain commercial-bank services, balance-sheet items, reserve and capital ratios, and liquidity, security and profitability objectives.
Explain how credit creation, central banking, deficit financing, quantitative easing and balance-of-payments changes alter money supply.
Assess policies for reducing inflation and their effectiveness.
Explain demand for money using liquidity-preference theory.
Explain interest-rate determination using loanable-funds and Keynesian theories.
Understand money and banking, including money supply, quantity theory, commercial banks, changes in money supply, inflation policies, money demand and interest-rate determination.
Explain objectives concerning inflation, balance of payments, unemployment, growth, development, sustainability and income or wealth redistribution.
Understand policy objectives concerning inflation, the balance of payments, unemployment, growth, development, sustainability, and income and wealth redistribution.
Explain the relationship between money’s domestic purchasing power and its external exchange value.
Explain links between the balance of payments and inflation.
Explain the relationship between economic growth and inflation.
Explain the relationship between economic growth and the balance of payments.
Explain traditional and expectations-augmented Phillips curves, including short- and long-run relationships.
Analyse relationships between money values, the balance of payments, inflation, growth and unemployment, including traditional and expectations-augmented Phillips curves.

topics.title: 10.3 Effectiveness of policy options to meet all macroeconomic objectives

outcomes.text: Evaluate fiscal, monetary, supply-side, exchange-rate and international-trade policies against different macroeconomic objectives.
Explain conflicts and difficulties resulting from macroeconomic policy outcomes.
Assess the possibility of government failure in macroeconomic policymaking.
Evaluate how fiscal, monetary, supply-side, exchange-rate and trade policies meet macroeconomic objectives, including conflicts and government failure.
